title: Assemblage and Found Objects
welcome_lead: From Duchamp's urinal to contemporary assemblage — when objects become art.
meta_desc: A-Level Art & Design: assemblage, found objects, and the readymade tradition.

walkthroughs.body_html: In 1917, Marcel Duchamp submitted Fountain, a porcelain urinal signed 'R. Mutt', to a New York exhibition. The gesture proposed that selection by the artist, not handcraft, defines art.
Kurt Schwitters' Merz collages (1920s), Joseph Cornell's poetic boxes (1930s-60s), Robert Rauschenberg's Combines (1950s) and Damien Hirst's vitrines all extend the assemblage tradition.
At A-Level, assemblage rewards conceptual rigour: object choice must carry meaning. Provenance, scale, juxtaposition and installation context all become carriers of significance.
